GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: OpenCode 2 keeps one long-lived server across many sessions and supports config reload without a process restart, while the vvoc configuration can change between releases and while work is in flight. The feature must let a session family keep the models, plugin policy, and orchestration profile it bound at its first workload, across /reload and across a full server restart, and must change that binding only when the user explicitly asks with --force. The original implementation attempted this with a full effective-vvoc capture and a durable store, but coupled integrity to the package-version-bound $schema URL, persisted credentials in plaintext, failed the entire plugin load on the first invalid family, and grew without bound. The redesign keeps the durable guarantee that was explicitly requested, but replaces the full-document capture with a content-addressed behaviour-relevant projection (no credentials, no version-derived fields) plus a tiny per-family pointer, and adds an explicit force path. It also relocates the orchestration policy from the system prefix to the request tail so a deliberate policy change does not invalidate the whole provider prefix cache, which is prefix-cached by every provider. The in-process binding remains the working facade; the durable layer only preserves the binding across process boundaries.

Alternatives.Alternative: In-memory-only binding: bind families in process memory, lose the binding on server restart, and rebind to the current configuration on the next workload. Simplest and removes the entire bug class, but rejected because the user requires bindings to survive a server restart and to reset only through --force.

Full durable policy snapshot addressed by config revision: one immutable snapshot per behaviour-relevant config revision containing the full policy document minus credentials and version fields, with a per-family pointer. This is the chosen shape; it preserves the strongest fidelity (models, toggles, orchestration profile) while remaining version-independent and credential-free.

In-place hotfix of the current store: keep the structure but exclude $schema from integrity, add per-family fault isolation, stop writing credentials, and add garbage collection. Rejected as an architecture because it preserves the duplicated derived data, the two-phase candidate machinery, and the fragile coupling between storage layout and consumer expectations.

Keep capture in the system prefix and accept a single full context re-read per policy change. Rejected as the default because policy changes are a recurring, company-relevant cost concern; kept as a documented fallback if the tail-injection host probe fails.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: The exact behaviour-relevant projection field list (which model-selection, toggle, and orchestration fields are canonical) is finalized during planning after inventorying every configFor consumer.

The garbage-collection policy details (startup sweep versus event-driven, retention of snapshots referenced by long-lived families) are finalized during planning against the observed session-deletion event shape.

Whether a missing or corrupt binding rebinds to the current configuration with a warning or refuses the family is specified as rebind-with-warning for absent or corrupt data, to avoid bricking sessions; if the implementation finds a case where silent adoption would hide a security-relevant change, that case is surfaced separately.
The exact tail injection shape (added part on the last message versus an appended transient message) is chosen from the host probe result.
Release sequencing: no separate hotfix is planned; the host stays on 2.1.3 until the redesign release, and a minimal 2.1.5 is cut only if an earlier upgrade becomes necessary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Package upgrade regression: a capture written under 2.1.3 was rejected by 2.1.4 code because normalizeStrictVvocConfig rewrote $schema and integrity then mismatched; under the redesign the snapshot excludes $schema and credentials, so the same upgrade reads the binding unchanged. Probe evidence from the live host confirmed the failure mode before this change.

Restart continuity: a family is bound under preset A; the user applies preset B and restarts the server; the family rehydrates preset A from its pointer and snapshot, while a newly created session binds preset B.

Worker model swap: during a long orchestrated run the implementer model hits a rate or cost limit; the user runs a force command that re-resolves worker bindings to a new model; only sessions whose resolved selection changed are switched, and the root session keeps its model and cached prefix.

Emergency toggle: the secrets-redaction plugin misbehaves mid-session; the user disables it with --force; the affected family adopts the new toggle while unrelated families keep their binding; the known cache cost from changing rendered history is accepted as a deliberate emergency action.

Orchestration switch: after designing in a single-session profile, the user forces the orchestrated profile in the same session without moving context; because the policy block lives in the request tail, only the tail changes and the cached prefix survives.

Store corruption: a pointer or snapshot is truncated; plugin load succeeds, other families are unaffected, and the affected family rebinds to the current configuration with a bounded diagnostic instead of bricking the project.
One-time upgrade rebind: existing snapshots are invalid and credential-bearing, so they are ignored; each existing family rebinds once to the current configuration and is durable afterwards.

Execution finding: the transient orchestration policy part must be appended only when the last request message is a user turn; appending into a trailing tool or assistant message corrupted the provider payload shape and aborted multi-tool turns, which surfaced as failing hashline-edit, spec-guard, and tool-history-compaction acceptance rows until fixed.

Execution finding: the model guard must expect the host-resolved family-qualified variant for explicit selections and accept the native source-variant form as equivalent, otherwise the first request of an explicitly created session is refused.

Execution residual: the host creates no model request for a child session prompted after a worktree move in the acceptance harness, so the moved-fork provider payload is recorded but not asserted; lineage, capture, and session-model assertions remain enforced.
